acceptance_checks.description: sha256 over the sorted set of non-blank raw lines recomputed from bronze matches the same hash computed over the file the legacy script actually consumed (order-insensitive line-set hash, not a whole-file byte hash; blank lines carry no records and are excluded on both sides)
per-file count of schema-valid silver rows matches the count of legacy PSV rows minus rows the legacy script silently mishandled (planted anomalies)

sha256 over the sorted set of pipe-delimited silver rows re-rendered in legacy PSV format (trailing-space trim, %.2f amount, YYYY-MM-DD slice) is byte-identical to the same hash over the legacy script's valid output rows
count and amount-in-cents totals per currency and record type recomputed from ow_tp.silver.custbill_parsed_cnvparse match totals computed from legacy valid PSV output, to the cent
overall valid row count and grand total cents match legacy valid output to the cent
distinct source files in bronze equals the number of files the legacy run consumed
quarantine row count equals the number of planted anomalies (one row-level defect per bad record, one file-level trailer mismatch row)

planted_anomalies.description: CUSTBILL_CNVPARSE_001.dat body row 7 carries bill_date 20241131 (Nov 31 does not exist); legacy emits 2024-11-31 silently. Converted job must quarantine it with reason invalid_calendar_date and exclude it from silver.
CUSTBILL_CNVPARSE_002.dat body row 13 carries amount 0000012X4567; legacy awk coerces it to 0.12 silently. Converted job must quarantine it with reason nonnumeric_amount and exclude it from silver.

CUSTBILL_CNVPARSE_003.dat trailer claims 53 records vs 50 body rows; legacy only logs the discrepancy. Converted job must emit a file-level quarantine row with reason trailer_count_mismatch (valid body rows still load to silver, matching legacy output).

encoding_policy.input_encoding: ASCII (generator emits ASCII-only fixed-width records); files are landed as raw bytes
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: transport is a Files API PUT of the exact bytes the legacy script consumed; integrity is verified by the input_sha256 checks, an order-insensitive sha256 over the non-blank raw line set recomputed from bronze (line reordering or blank-line loss in transport is outside this check's coverage); parsing slices fixed columns and never decodes-then-re-encodes
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: a non-ASCII or otherwise invalid byte cannot make the job fail or silently drop data: the line still lands in bronze byte-for-byte and, if it breaks field validation, is attributed to quarantine with a reason rather than lost

malformed_record_policy.details: Input is fixed-width, so a stray '|' inside a field is data, not a delimiter; it flows through to silver exactly as the legacy cut/paste chain emitted it. NULL or missing source values never fail open into a plausible-looking row: silver admits a row only when every field passes its explicit predicate (non-empty id after trailing-space trim — CUST-ID is PIC X(10), so shorter space-padded ids are legal and pass exactly as legacy emitted them; an all-blank id is quarantined as invalid_cust_id — 12-digit amount, real calendar date, ccy in USD/EUR/GBP, rt in 01/02); anything else becomes a quarantine row with an explicit reason. Short lines yield empty/NULL slices which fail those predicates and are quarantined, never defaulted.

empty_input_semantics.details: A run with no landed input rewrites bronze/silver/quarantine for the namespace as empty (INSERT OVERWRITE of an empty scan), mirroring the legacy behaviour that a batch with no CUSTBILL*.dat files produces no PSV output; prior output does not survive into the next batch's result set.

notes: Legacy loop processes every CUSTBILL*.dat present in incoming/ in one cron pass and reports once per batch; the converted job is a single manual-trigger batch job over the namespace landing dir (/Volumes/ow_tp/bronze/landing/cnvparse/parse), and the golden comparison is per-batch with per-file checks inside it. All-blank customer ids, unknown currency or unknown record type values are additionally quarantined (invalid_cust_id / unknown_currency / unknown_record_type) to make the silver schema contract explicit, and a TRL line whose count digits do not parse is quarantined as unparseable_trailer via try_cast (the legacy script just logs 'trailer says ?'; a corrupted trailer never fails the job); the deterministic generator never emits any of these, so they appear in no baseline check.
